effects.target: Assume the form of a Small or Medium fey. Your base speed becomes the new form's, to a maximum of 60 feet. You gain any of the listed movement modes, senses and special abilities that the chosen form actually has, and you also gain that form's weaknesses. An ability that depends on an item transforms the nearest counterpart in your worn gear. Spells the creature has as spell-like abilities need no verbal or somatic components from you and cannot be countered, though you still cast them as normal for your class.
Small fey: +2 size bonus to Dexterity and Constitution. Medium fey: +2 size bonus to Strength and Constitution. An aquatic form lets you breathe both air and water.

fey-form-i.notes: The size bonuses are an either/or between two rows, so they are NOT emitted as ability_mod specs — doing so would stack Small's +2 Dex with Medium's +2 Str on the same caster. Every other listed ability is conditional on which fey the caster picks, which the vocabulary cannot gate on.

Tiny fey: +6 size bonus to Dexterity, -2 penalty to Strength. Large fey: +4 size bonus to Strength and Constitution, -2 penalty to Dexterity.
If the chosen form is immune to mind-affecting effects or to poison, you gain a +4 resistance bonus on saves against those effects instead.

This spell's own description states no numbers — it says only 'functions as fly, save that it can target numerous creatures and lasts longer'. The 60/40 feet, the maneuverability and the descent were READ OUT OF `fly`'s own prose in the corpus, not guessed. SEPARATE BUG FOUND WHILE READING, NOT IN THIS PARTITION: `fly` itself currently carries a converted top-level effect of `damage 1d6 untyped, scales full`. It is the same class of defect as the teleport mishap example and should be re-read.

effects.target: Whether or not the touch attack hits, the hook drags you in a straight line to a square adjacent to the target, provoking attacks of opportunity as normal. It holds you up during the movement, so you can cross a pit or chasm or change elevation, and you land on your feet unharmed if the path is clear.

If the line of effect passes through a space too small for your body, such as a portcullis or arrow slit, the hook pulls you to that spot and you take damage as though you had fallen the distance travelled. If you are restrained you are pulled to the limit of your restraints, which do not break. The spell does not guarantee a safe landing space — if the target is flying or on a ledge with no room, you begin to fall on arrival.
When used with the spell combat class ability, make your melee attack from either your starting position or your ending position.

force-hook-charge.notes: This damage IS emitted as a top-level spec, unlike most in this partition: the spell's own targets line is 'you + creature or object (1 within range)', so the creature the caster aims at is exactly who takes it, at cast time. It is gated on a ranged touch attack rather than a save, which the vocabulary cannot express, so that condition is recorded in the note. `scaling` is omitted because 1 point per caster level has no die, and the scaling schema requires a real die size. The falling damage in the too-small-gap case is taken by the CASTER in an edge case and is not converted. `element` is omitted because the corpus already derives it as force.

effects.target: Create a +1 longsword of pure force sized for you, which you may wield or hand to another creature like any other longsword. It becomes a +2 longsword at 8th level and a +3 longsword at 13th.
It cannot be attacked or harmed by physical attacks, but dispel magic, disintegrate, a sphere of annihilation or a rod of cancellation affects it.

The first time the sword strikes a creature with spell resistance you must make a caster level check against that SR. Failure dispels the spell; success gives the weapon full effect against that creature for the duration.

force-sword.notes: The sword's damage is the longsword's, dealt when someone swings it, not damage this spell deals — so no damage spec. The +1/+2/+3 is a weapon enhancement bonus on a created item rather than a bonus granted to a creature, and it steps with caster level, so no combat_mod either. `element` is omitted because the corpus already derives it as force.

effects.target: Create an immobile, invisible prison of force — your choice of a 20-foot barred cage or a 10-foot windowless cell. Creatures inside are contained; if a creature is too big to fit, the spell automatically fails.

Barred cage: half-inch bands with half-inch gaps. Anything able to pass through such a gap escapes. You cannot attack a creature inside with a weapon unless it fits between the bars, and even then the creature has cover. All spells and breath weapons pass through freely. Windowless cell: six solid walls of force with no way in or out.

Teleportation and astral travel escape it, but the barrier extends into the Ethereal Plane and blocks ethereal travel. It resists dispel magic though mage's disjunction works, its walls have hardness 30 and 20 hit points per caster level, disintegrate destroys it automatically, and contact with a sphere of annihilation or rod of cancellation destroys it instantly.

forcecage.notes: Note a corpus discrepancy: the derived save reads 'Reflex negates', but this description never mentions a saving throw — containment depends on size and on fitting through the gaps. No save_gate is invented on the strength of the derived field alone. `element` is omitted because the corpus derives it as force.
